title: Finite negative twists generate the projective-space derived category
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$, with twists [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Put $T=\bigoplus_{i=0}^n\mathcal O_X(-i)$ in degree zero. In $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $T$ is a weak generator [def-pc-generators]: for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, if $\operatorname{Hom}(T,K[q])=0$ for all $q\in\mathbf Z$, then $K\simeq0$.

proof.text: Fix $K$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(T,K[q])=0$ for all $q$. In the ambient $D(\mathcal O_X)$ form $\mathcal S=\{F:\operatorname{Hom}(F,K[q])=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathbf Z\}$. Apply [lem-sf-shift-stable-left-orthogonal] to the shift-stable class of all $K[q]$: $\mathcal S$ is strictly full and triangulated. For each summand $L_i=\mathcal O_X(-i)$, a map $f:L_i\to K[q]$ equals $(f\circ\pi_i)\circ\iota_i=0$, so $L_i\in\mathcal S$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. A map out of a finite direct sum is determined by its restrictions to the summands; hence every finite direct sum of objects of $\mathcal S$ (in particular of twists already shown to lie in $\mathcal S$) lies in $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tag 0A9V, perfect-lemma-generator-P1, proof; Tags 0BQS and 0BQR for the two geometric inputs.

proof.text: Prove by strong induction on $m\geq0$ that $\mathcal O_X(-m)\in\mathcal S$. The cases $m\leq n$ were just proved. For $m\geq n+1$, apply [lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-koszul-sequence] with $a=-m$. Omit its leftmost term and place the remaining terms $\mathcal O_X(-m+j)^{\oplus\binom{n+1}{j}}$ in degrees $j-1$, $1\leq j\leq n+1$, to get a bounded complex $C$. Its terms lie in $\mathcal S$ by induction, since $0\leq m-j<m$. The augmentation $\mathcal O_X(-m)[0]\to C$ induces an isomorphism on degree-zero cohomology and both sides have zero cohomology in all other degrees, by exactness of the sequence. It is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-complex-triangulated-devissage], $C\in\mathcal S$; closure under isomorphisms gives the induction step.

source.place: Tag 0A9V, perfect-lemma-generator-P1, proof; Tags 0BQS and 0BQR for the two geometric inputs.

proof.text:
Put $L_m=\mathcal O_X(-m)$. It is locally free of rank one by [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so is perfect. Applying [lem-sc-finite-locally-free-derived-hom] with target $\mathcal O_X[0]$ identifies its derived dual with the ordinary line-bundle dual. On $U_i$ the dual basis of $e_i^{(-m)}$ transforms by $(x_i/x_j)^m$; thus $L_m^\vee=\mathcal O_X(m)=\mathcal O_X(1)^{\otimes m}$. The unbounded evaluation isomorphism of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], the global Hom identification [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], and [lem-sc-global-hom-shifted-hypercohomology] with shift indices $(0,q)$ give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L_m,K[q])\cong H^q\bigl(X,K\otimes^L\mathcal O_X(m)\bigr).$$
Tensor symmetry here is the chain isomorphism $t\otimes k\mapsto k\otimes t$, with no sign since the line lies in degree zero. These groups vanish for every $m\geq0$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$ by the induction. The global comparison is applied on the Zariski site (small in a fixed sufficiently large universe); all these cited results allow arbitrary unbounded $K$.

source.place: Tag 0A9V, perfect-lemma-generator-P1, proof; Tags 0BQS and 0BQR for the two geometric inputs.

proof.text: The line bundle $\mathcal O_X(1)$ is ample in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: the finitely many affine opens $U_i=D_+(x_i)$ cover $X$. The coordinate $x_i$ defines a section $s_i$ whose expression on $U_j$ is $(x_i/x_j)e_j^{(1)}$. The transition rule of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] glues these expressions, and their nonvanishing locus is precisely $U_i$. This finite affine section cover verifies both clauses of the cited definition of ampleness.

source.place: Tag 0A9V, perfect-lemma-generator-P1, proof; Tags 0BQS and 0BQR for the two geometric inputs.

proof.text: If $K\not\simeq0$, apply [lem-sfb-ample-twist-hypercohomology-detection] to $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X(1)$, which step 4 proved ample. It supplies $m\geq0$ and $q$ with $H^q(X,K\otimes^L\mathcal O_X(1)^{\otimes m})\neq0$, contrary to step 3. Therefore $K\simeq0$, exactly the weak-generator criterion [def-pc-generators].
